pearls: A cigarette's **length** roughly matches the time needed to desensitize α4β2 receptors; shorter wastes pleasure, longer adds nothing (p548).
Addiction can start with the **first cigarette** (anterior cingulate activation lasting about a month in animals); craving appears within a month of repeated use (p548).
Smoking is very common in psychiatric practice: **40–50%** of psychopharmacology patients, **60–85%** in ADHD, schizophrenia and bipolar; only about 10% are proactively offered treatment (p547–548).
Changes may be lifelong: a **"molecular memory"** persists in long-abstinent ex-smokers (p551).
Quit rates with **bupropion** are about half those of varenicline (p553).
Acts at α4β2 receptors on **VTA** dopamine, glutamate and GABA neurons (Fig 13-12); it is selective for the α4β2 subtype (p552).

pearls: Known as **"Molly"** (for "molecular") as well as Ecstasy; once popular in clubs and raves (p358, p569).
Only **pure MDMA** is studied in therapy; street drug is often cut with bath salts, methamphetamine, dextromethorphan, ketamine or cocaine, and taken with marijuana and alcohol (p358).
Rationale in PTSD: an **empathic** state may suit painful-memory work better than psilocybin's mystical or ketamine's dissociative state (p574).
Aimed at patients for whom first-line **exposure therapy** fails or is too painful (p574).
Contrast with amphetamine: amphetamine is mainly an NDRI releasing dopamine; MDMA is mainly a SERT inhibitor releasing **serotonin** (p356, Fig 7-87).

pearls: **CB1** is denser in brain; **CB2** is mostly on peripheral immune cells (p563).

"Medical marijuana" is an **unprocessed plant** (~500 chemicals) with variable content and contaminants, so not a standard prescription drug (p564).
Evidence for benefit in anxiety, PTSD and Tourette is **limited**; epilepsy, dementia and addiction **insufficient** (p566–567).
